rules.name: r3_nondivisible_threshold
rules.description_text: Domain: r = 3 and no a_i divisible by 3. Let F = sum over i of floor(a_i/3) and S = number of i with a_i = 2 mod 3. Then P = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q [b]_{q^3} is weakly unimodal exactly when b <= 1 + F + 2*floor(S/6). An equivalent form uses D = sum(a_i - 1) = 3F + S: unimodal iff 3(b-1) <= D - (S mod 6). Outside the domain (some a_i divisible by 3), predict returns True by Cor. 4.3 of arXiv:2605.12822; that case is cited, not proved here, and domain() excludes it.

proofs.statement: Let r=3, k>=0, a_1..a_k>=1 with no a_i divisible by 3, and b>=1. Put F = sum floor(a_i/3) and S = #{a_i = 2 mod 3}. Then [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q [b]_{q^3} is weakly unimodal if and only if b <= 1 + F + 2*floor(S/6). Equivalently 3(b-1) <= D - (S mod 6), where D = sum(a_i - 1). The proof covers both directions for all parameters, with no box restriction.

path_id: A1' (E2): probabilistic / Fourier formalization via roots-of-unity filter

rules.name: E2_exact (Theorem A: exact Fourier criterion, proved)
rules.description_text: Let D = sum(a_i - 1) and K = D + 1 - r(b+1). If r divides some a_i, predict unimodal. Otherwise: (1) compute the coefficients p_m of p(q) = prod [a_i]_q; (2) for u >= 0 set d_u = (p_u - p_{u-1}) + d_{u-r}, with d_u = 0 for u < 0. These are the power-series coefficients of p(q)(1-q)/(1-q^r). (3) Compute the residue imbalance tau_rho for rho = 0..r-1: reduce prod [a_i mod r]_q modulo q^r - 1 to get class sums f_rho, then set tau_rho = f_rho - f_{(rho-1) mod r}. Equivalently, tau_rho = (1/r) sum_{j=1}^{r-1} zeta^{-j rho}(1 - zeta^j) p(zeta^j) with zeta = e^{2 pi i/r}. Extend tau r-periodically to all integers. (4) Let E_u = d_u - tau_u, so E_u = -tau_u for u < 0. Predict unimodal iff E_u >= d_{K-u} for every integer u with K/2 < u <= D+1-r. Because tau is periodic, negative u only need checking for u >= -r. Equivalent form (Theorem A'): write p = [r]_q Q + R and let c = max{c in 0..r-1 : tau_c > 0}. Then P is unimodal iff all three hold: (N) r(b-1) <= D+1-2c; (Q) Q_u >= 0 for u > max(K, K/2); (P) Q_u - Q_{K-u} >= tau_{K-u} for K/2 < u <= K.

rules.name: E2_closed_small (closed form for r<=3 or at most 3 nontrivial factors)
rules.description_text: Domain: r <= 3, or at most three a_i are >= 2. Let S = sum floor(a_i/r). Predict unimodal iff r divides some a_i, or one of the following holds. If r = 3: b <= 1 + S + 2*floor(n2/6), where n2 = #{i : a_i = 2 mod 3}. Otherwise (r = 2, or at most three a_i >= 2): b <= 1 + S. The 'only if' direction is proved in every case: Thm B, Cor D1, Cor E and Cor R3. The 'if' direction is proved whenever r(b+1) >= D+1 (Cor S1(a), R3(c)). For r(b+1) < D+1 the 'if' direction is conjectural; it holds throughout the fit box.
rules.fit_range: fit box restricted to the domain (15,525,600 instances)

rules.name: E2_threshold (explicit y*-threshold; ignores the rare pair obstructions)
rules.description_text: If r divides some a_i, predict unimodal. Otherwise compute d_u and tau as in E2_exact, and let y* = max{u in Z : d_u < tau_u}; search u in [-r, D+1-r]. Predict unimodal iff r(b+1) + 2y* <= D+1. This is exact whenever r(b+1) >= D+1 (Corollary A1). Its only errors in the box are the 133 instances where condition (P) fails; there the set of unimodal b is not an initial segment.

rules.name: E2_residue (Theorem B Fourier threshold; a proved necessary condition)
rules.description_text: If r divides some a_i, predict unimodal. Otherwise let c = max{c in 0..r-1 : tau_c > 0}. In closed form, tau_c = (2/r) sum_{j=1}^{r-1} sin(pi j/r) A_j sin(pi j (D_pi+1-2c)/r), where A_j = prod_i sin(pi j t_i/r)/sin(pi j/r), t_i = a_i mod r and D_pi = sum(t_i - 1). Predict unimodal iff r(b-1) <= D+1-2c, i.e. b <= 1 + S + floor((D_pi+1-2c)/r). The condition is necessary (proved): there are 0 false negatives. It is exact when the quotient of p by [r]_q has nonnegative coefficients and (P) holds.

proofs.statement: Theorem A (exact criterion, all parameters). Let d be the power-series coefficients of p(q)(1-q)/(1-q^r), with d = 0 at negative indices. Let tau be the r-periodic tail of d, given by tau_rho = (1/r) sum_{j=1}^{r-1} zeta^{-j rho}(1-zeta^j) p(zeta^j), which depends only on the a_i mod r. Let E_u = d_u - tau_u and K = D+1-r(b+1). Then P is unimodal iff E_u >= d_{K-u} for all integers u with K/2 < u <= D+1-r. Theorem A' gives the equivalent split into (N), (Q) and (P). The key steps are the identity (1-q)P = (p/[r]_q)(1-q^{rb}) and the reflection d_x = tau_x + d_{D+1-r-x}.

Theorem B with Lemma F (necessary Fourier threshold). Suppose r divides no a_i, and let c = max{c in 0..r-1 : tau_c > 0}, where tau_c = (2/r) sum_j sin(pi j/r) A_j sin(pi j (D_pi+1-2c)/r) and A_j = prod_i sin(pi j t_i/r)/sin(pi j/r). If P is unimodal then r(b-1) <= D+1-2c, i.e. b <= 1+S+floor((D_pi+1-2c)/r). Lemma C: 2c <= D_pi+1. Lemma S: if p = [r]G + h with G >= 0 and h palindromic unimodal of degree D_h <= 2r-1, then the quotient Q is nonnegative. In that case, whenever r(b+1) >= D+1, the bound is exact.

Corollary D1 (necessity clause for k<=3, every r). Suppose r divides no a_i and at most three a_i are >= 2. If P is unimodal then b <= 1 + sum floor(a_i/r). The proof shows tau_{t_(2)-1} >= 1, where t_(2) is the median residue.
Corollary E (r=2, every k). If all a_i are odd and P is unimodal, then b <= 1+S. If moreover 2(b+1) >= D+1, then P is unimodal iff b <= 1+S.

Corollary R3 (r=3, every k). Suppose no a_i is divisible by 3, and let n2 = #{a_i = 2 mod 3}. (a) If P is unimodal then b <= 1+S+2*floor(n2/6). (b) The quotient of p by [3]_q is nonnegative; the certificate is (1+q)^6 = 1 + [3]_q q(6+9q+5q^2+q^3). (c) If 3(b+1) >= D+1, then P is unimodal iff b <= 1+S+2*floor(n2/6). (d) The necessity clause of Conjecture 5.4 for r=3 holds for a given a iff n2 <= 5. For every a with n2 >= 6, b0 = S-1+ceil((n2+1)/3) >= S+2 gives a unimodal P, an infinite family generalizing (1+q)^6(1+q^3).

Corollary S1 (sufficiency clause, partial). Suppose r divides no a_i and b <= 1+S. Then (N) and (Q) hold. Hence P is unimodal whenever additionally r(b+1) >= D+1. In general, b <= 1+S implies unimodality iff c_x >= c_{x-1} for rb <= x <= N/2, which is condition (P). NOT proved: (P) for b <= 1+S when r(b+1) < D+1. It holds throughout the fit box, where the baseline rule has 0 false positives.

rules.name: fine_table_small_bigres_d
rules.description_text: Drop the trivial factors a_i=1. If r divides some a_i, P is unimodal. Otherwise let F = sum floor(a_i/r) and d = b-1-F. If d<=0, P is unimodal. If d>=1, P is unimodal iff d is in E(r,S,Rb), where S = sorted multiset of the factors with 1<a_i<r and Rb = sorted multiset of (a_i mod r) over the factors a_i>r. E is a lookup table fitted on the full box (embedded in the file). It has 32,206 classes, and each takes one of four values: {} (19,025 classes), {1,2} (12,615), {1,2,3,4} (481) or {2} (85). A class missing from the table means E={}. The key uses only residues and min(a_i,r), so the table covers every a with at most 8 nontrivial factors and r<=6. Outside the box the rule assumes that, once S and Rb are fixed, F matters only through d.
rules.fit_range: whole fit box: r in 2..6, k<=8, a_i<=12, b<=60 (37,790,700 instances); domain(r,a): 2<=r<=6 and #(a_i>1)<=8

If d>=1, P is unimodal iff d is in E(r,R), where R = sorted multiset of a_i mod r over all a_i>1. E is a lookup table fitted on the box by majority vote (embedded). rules.name: E4-sufficient (proved, one-sided)
rules.description_text: predict(r,a,b) returns True iff b <= 1 + sum_i floor(a_i/r), or r divides some a_i. Otherwise it returns False. A True prediction is a theorem (proof.txt): P is then symmetric and weakly unimodal, for all r>=2, k>=1, a_i>=1, b>=1. A False prediction is NOT a claim: necessity is not asserted and is known to fail, e.g. r=3, a=(2,2,2,2,2,2), b=2. domain(r,a) is True everywhere. proofs.statement:
For all r>=2, k>=1, a_1..a_k>=1, b>=1: if b <= 1 + sum_i floor(a_i/r), or r | a_i for some i, then P(q) = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q [b]_{q^r} is symmetric and weakly unimodal. This is the full sufficiency half of Conj. 5.4.

Mechanism (Lambda / centred-chain decomposition, no residue-window sums): induction over the factors, using Clebsch-Gordan peeling [L][a'] = sum_{d<d0} q^d[L+a'-1-2d] + q^{d0}[L-d0][a'-d0] with d0 = min(s', e+1), where a' = r m' + s' and e = L - rM - 1. This writes A = prod[a_i] = U + V. Every U-piece is q^e[c]H with r | c and H a product of q-integers, all centred at D/2. Every V-piece is a centred chain q^j[L] with L >= r*sum floor(a_i/r) + 1. Each U-piece times [b]_{q^r} is symmetric unimodal: [c][b]_{q^r} = [r]_q([c/r]_x[b]_x)(q^r) and [r]_q[m]_{q^r} = [rm]_q. Each V-chain times [b]_{q^r} is unimodal because L >= r(b-1)+1. All pieces share the centre N/2, so their sum is symmetric unimodal.
